PAL/1.0 Protocol ​

The PAL/1.0 protocol is the control layer for Palexplorer — handling share negotiation, key exchange, sync, chat, and routing.

Envelope Format ​

Every message is wrapped in a signed envelope:

json
{
  "v": 1,
  "type": "share.offer",
  "from": "<sender-public-key-hex>",
  "to": "<recipient-public-key-hex>",
  "id": "<uuid-v4>",
  "ts": "<ISO-8601>",
  "payload": { ... },
  "sig": "<ed25519-detached-signature-hex>"
}

Signature: SHA-256(canonical_json(v, type, from, to, id, ts, payload)) signed with Ed25519.

Message Types ​

Discovery & Identity ​

TypeDirectionDescription
identity.announce→ serverPublish identity
identity.resolve→ serverRequest handle resolution
identity.response← serverResolved public key(s)
heartbeat→ serverKeepalive (5-min window)

Share Negotiation ​

TypeDirectionDescription
share.offer→ peerShare metadata + policy
share.accept← peerAccept + Curve25519 public key
share.key→ peerMagnet + wrapped encryption key
share.revoke→ peerRevoke access
share.policy.update→ peerUpdate live policy

Transfer Control ​

TypeDirectionDescription
transfer.request→ seederRequest download
transfer.authorize← seederAuthorize + magnet (policy enforced)
transfer.deny← seederDeny (expired/revoked/limit)
transfer.progress→ seederReport progress
transfer.complete→ seederConfirm completion
transfer.receipt← seederSigned proof of delivery

Sync ​

TypeDirectionDescription
sync.manifest↔Exchange file manifest
sync.diff→ peerComputed delta
sync.request→ peerRequest specific files
sync.conflict↔Signal conflict

Chat ​

TypeDirectionDescription
chat.message→ peerEncrypted message (crypto_box)
chat.ack← peerDelivery acknowledgment
chat.typing→ peerTyping indicator

Routing ​

TypeDirectionDescription
route.probe→ peerTest connectivity
route.probe.response← peerLatency + reachability
relay.request→ serverRequest TURN allocation
relay.allocated← serverTURN credentials + limits

Policy Enforcement ​

Policies are evaluated on transfer.request:

  • Expiry time
  • Max downloads
  • Recipient whitelist
  • IP restrictions (CIDR)
  • Time windows (schedule)
  • Bandwidth limit (TURN relay level)
